chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said:

Indeed, Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bought a house and ordered one of his slaves to move into it, and said: 'Your home is narrow.' So he said: 'My father had built this house.' So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'If your father was foolish, it is befitting that you become like him.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam Al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَوْلًى: A slave or freed slave under one's patronage

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam's comment about the slave's father reveal about family traits and wisdom in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) demonstrates the virtue of generosity and social care by purchasing a home for his slave, Ali ibn Yaqteen, to alleviate his cramped living conditions. The Imam’s witty remark regarding the slave's father—implying that foolishness is hereditary—serves as a subtle scholarly commentary on the transmission of character traits (*khuluq*) within families, a theme often explored in Shia biographical literature (*rijal*). This incident underscores the Imam’s practical leadership and his ability to blend material benevolence with sharp intellectual insight.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> bought a house and ordered a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> that he transfers to it and said: ‘Your home is narrow’. So he said, ‘My father had built the house’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If your father was stupid is it befitting that you become similar to him?’
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, purchased a house and instructed one of his Mawla’ to move in saying, ‘Your house is congested.’ He said, ‘My father has established this house.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If your father was dimwitted, is it proper that you also be like him?”’
